subject: Renewal: ZenFalls — Split Commit + Temporary Price guard
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@zenfalls.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@zenfalls.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: ZenFalls — split commit + temporary price guard

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for the earlier conversation. We're kicking off renewal planning and want to explore a short-term price hold while we finalize our capacity forecast for Q3–Q4. High-level ask: can Redwood offer a 90‑day price guard at current rates while we commit to an expanded total commit split across two billing periods (60% in Q3, 40% in Q4)? We had a couple of unplanned spikes in Q1 (attached usage) and want to avoid a surprise step‑up in unit price when we renew.

Specifics we care about:
- Price guard window: 90 days from renewal effective date
- Commit structure: total committed units increase ~45% year-over-year, split 60/40 over two quarters
- Overage treatment: rolling credits vs. per-token billing (we prefer credits)
- Amendment mechanics: short form amendment + DocuSign

Can you confirm whether this is workable and what tradeoffs (discounts / credits / term length) Redwood would need? Happy to jump on a call this week — Priya from procurement is cc'd.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform & Ops
ZenFalls

Attachments:
- ZenFalls_MonthlyUsage_Q12027.csv (CSV)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@zenfalls.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: ZenFalls — split commit + temporary price guard

Hi Sanjay —

Appreciate the context and the usage file — that helps a lot. High level, we can structure something close to what you described but with a couple of firming points from our side:

Proposal (summary):
- Temporary price guard: 90 days at current hosted unit rate for the model(s) on the attached usage, starting from the amendment effective date.
- Commit: 45% uplift year-over-year with a 60/40 split across two quarterly invoices (Q3/Q4). We will model the commit as a single annual commitment for your account but allow phased billing as requested.
- Credits: overage during the 90-day window to be issued as one-time usage credits (applied to next invoice) rather than immediate per-token billing; credits will be capped at 15% of the committed volume during that window.
- Discount / concession: to accommodate the split-billing and the short guard window, Redwood will extend a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to 2% of the uplifted committed value (applied across the first two invoices).
- Operational: Redwood will issue a short amendment (two pages) and DocuSign link. We will include an explicit 30-day review clause to revisit commit sizing after the 90-day guard.

Open items for your procurement team: payment terms (net 30 vs net 45), whether the credit cap is acceptable, and whether you want the guard to apply to all models or only production model(s).

If that looks directionally right I can loop in Finance for final sign-off. Want me to prepare the amendment draft (v1) and send a DocuSign?

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Draft_AMENDMENT_v2.docx (planning draft)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@zenfalls.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: ZenFalls — split commit + temporary price guard

Thanks Mateo / Sanjay —

I like the approach but want to tighten the economics a touch to protect our unit economics while still giving ZenFalls certainty. Proposed adjustments:
- Reduce the uplift credit from 2% to 1.25% of the uplifted committed value (still applied across the first two invoices).
- Keep the 90-day guard but limit the model scope to production endpoints only (saves us on exploratory traffic). We can expand the scope in the 30-day review if you share endpoint tags.
- Move the overage cap to 12% of committed volume during the window (instead of 15%).

Karthik / Grace — could you weigh in on whether finance will accept net 45 payment for the first two invoices in exchange for the credit? If not, net 30 is standard.

Sanjay — if you can confirm acceptance of the narrower scope and credit change, I'll sign off on the amendment wording and we can DocuSign.

—Vanessa
VP Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Menon <priya.menon@zenfalls.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@zenfalls.com>, ZenFalls Procurement <procurement@zenfalls.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T11:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: ZenFalls — split commit + temporary price guard

Vanessa / Mateo —

Thanks for the clear proposal. Procurement is ok with the structure in principle. A few asks before we finalize:
1) Please include a simple sentence in the amendment that the 90-day price guard is not a cap on Redwood's right to market-based changes beyond the guard window (we will accept language, just want clarity).
2) DocuSign: please send the amendment via DocuSign and include a summary of invoice timing (we prefer the 60/40 invoice dates aligned to the quarter boundaries).
3) We can accept the reduced credit (1.25%) but would like the overage cap at 12% as Vanessa suggested.

Regarding payment terms: ZenFalls prefers net 45 for the first two invoices to help align cashflow given internal billing cycles; after that we can move to net 30. If Redwood requires net 30 up front we may need to reduce the credit further.

If you can share a DocuSign link by EOD tomorrow we will review and route for signature.

Thanks,
Priya Menon
Sr. Procurement Manager
ZenFalls

Related: procurement asked for a formal invoice schedule and a copy of the amendment to send to accounting.
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Menon <priya.menon@zenfalls.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@zenfalls.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T16:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: ZenFalls — split commit + temporary price guard

Priya / Sanjay —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Finance reviewed and we can accept the terms with the following guardrails:
- Credit: 1.25% of uplifted committed value applied pro rata across the first two invoices.
- Overage credits cap: 12% during the 90-day window. Any overage beyond that will be billed at standard per-token rates; we will include a reconciliation clause.
- Payment terms: Redwood will accept net 45 for the first two invoices as requested, with an automatic move to net 30 thereafter.

Action items next steps (I'll own):
1) Mateo will send the final amendment (v3) through DocuSign with the agreed language and invoice schedule (60/40 aligned to quarter boundaries).
2) Mateo to include a one-paragraph review clause and the exact model scope (production endpoints only).
3) Accounting — please expect an invoice schedule and amendment; ZenFalls procurement to confirm signers.

Mateo — please send the DocuSign link when ready and I'll mark the deal for legal/finance release in our system (Deal: ZFL-2027-041).

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Finance Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Draft_AMENDMENT_v2.docx
